### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **24** documentable anchor(s).

**20** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`.

⛔ **14** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **2** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **10** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `03759c298100af0d13bfdec4c5e30135e6cea5ef` — the merge of head `0ea49ba4c73287f7e78aa7db68f439ec29a3d96f` into base `2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 03759c298100af0d13bfdec4c5e30135e6cea5ef && git checkout 03759c298100af0d13bfdec4c5e30135e6cea5ef
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 0ea49ba4c73287f7e78aa7db68f439ec29a3d96f && git checkout -B drift-repro 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2 && git merge --no-ff 0ea49ba4c73287f7e78aa7db68f439ec29a3d96f

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 2ad42b5d056322b179fbf7decb68731831e3b4f2` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**What I checked (holds):**
- **The card is delivered whole.** #35256 asks for three things: run the connector lookup on a draft flow, surface it on the draft verdict in a shape its consumers read, and pin an unknown connector action. All three are in the diff. The advisory uses the gate-issue shape. Studio's draft read and `mcp-authoring.ts` `verdictOf` already pass `judgement.advisories` through unchanged, so neither consumer needed an edit. `Fixes` is right.
- **One shared judgement.** I read the `build-probes.ts` diff line by line. `unresolvedConnectorSteps` keeps the probe's three lookups in the same order: `resolveConnectorInstanceFor`, `resolveConnectorAction`, then `getConnectorDegradedReason`. A lookup that throws still judges nothing. The `message` and `fix` templates are byte-equal to the removed ones. `userMessage` is `buildProbeUserMessage(...)` with the same params, which is exactly what the old `say` closure called. `labelIn` reads the same `label` with the same locale ladder. The probe maps each step back to the same code, severity, artifact and `ref`, and still uses `opts.packageId ?? null`. Its own pins pass unchanged.
- **The step path is correct for regions too.** `collectFlowGraphs` (spec control-flow.zod.ts) keeps list identity when nothing is dropped, and `graph.path` is anchored on the raw list. So `listed.indexOf(node)` resolves inside a region, for example `nodes[0].config.body.nodes[2]`.
- **Advisory only.** `draftPublishJudgement` appends the advisories only for `singular === 'flow'`, and only to `advisories`. `refusals` is built exactly as before. `draftPublishVerdict`, which feeds `_diagnostics`, returns `.refusals` only, so it does not move. `judgeRuntimeAuthoringRules` and `assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` have no edit. The body judged is the same `storedFlowVerdictBody` the promotion judges. The change is a hoisted `const`.
- **Host member.** `servicesRegistry: () => this.getServicesRegistry` is a forwarding reader that is read per call. `draftConnectorAdvisories` catches a throwing registry and refuses an engine without `resolveConnectorAction`. `protocol.ts` is 11705 lines. I ran `pnpm check:facade-delegation-only` on the head: exit 0, within ceiling. The merged `const` line is the only other edit.
- **Changeset, sentence by sentence** (`.changeset/35256-draft-connector-advisory.md`, `patch`):
  - "The publish's build probe … warns, after a flow is published …": holds, unchanged behaviour.
  - "The draft verdict (`draftPublishJudgement`, read by Studio's draft review and by the MCP draft tools' `verdict.advisories`) now says the same thing before Publish is pressed: one advisory per such step, rule …, `severity: 'warning'`, located at the step …, the probe's `message`, its `fix` as the `hint`, its user sentence in the read's language": holds against `draftConnectorAdvisories`. The path is pinned at `nodes.1.connectorConfig` on the draft read.
  - "It is never a refusal: … still saves, reads valid, and publishes": holds and is pinned (`assertRuntimeAuthoringRules` and `publishMetaItem` case).
  - "The publish gate's own answer is unchanged, and the build probe reports exactly what it reported before; both doors now ask one shared lookup": holds (see above).
  - "A host without an automation service, or one without the connector lookups, judges nothing, as the probe does": holds and is pinned.
- **Tests I ran on fb7a69f8** (after `pnpm turbo run build --filter=@objectstack/metadata-protocol^...`, 12/12 tasks, exit 0): `protocol.draft-publish-verdict.test.ts`, `build-probes-landed-data.test.ts` and `build-probes-user-message.test.ts` together, 143/143.
- **Positive controls (each restored with `git checkout --`, then `git status` empty):**
  - Advisory join disabled (`false && singular === 'flow'`): the #35256 describe went red, 4 failed / 2 passed. The two silence pins stayed green, as they should.
  - Step path off by one (`indexOf(node) + 1`): 1 failed / 5 passed.
  - Draft lookups asked with `null` instead of `draft.packageId`: 2 failed / 4 passed.

**Non-blocking notes:**
1. **The probe's `message` text is not pinned verbatim.** I changed the shared template's last word ("fails." → "failz."). All 143 tests across the three files stayed green. The one-judgement pin compares the two doors to each other, and the landed probe pins read the code and the user sentence. The words are byte-equal by my read of the diff, so nothing is wrong today. This gap was there before the PR and is wider now that two doors share the text.
2. **Region paths are unpinned.** Only a top-level step's path is pinned. The region path (`nodes[N].config.body.nodes[M]…`) is correct by reading but has no case. The changeset names only the `flows[0].nodes[N].connectorConfig` form, and the PR body's acceptance notes cover the nested one.
3. **Clause-② spelling.** The line is spelled `yes — widening: …`, not `yes (widening)`, so `clause2-line.mjs` reads `yes` with no arm. That is still non-breaking and still lands in the release notes' "new capabilities" section, as the body says. It is copied from the claim.

**Landing:** not governed. Clause-② widening. The seat's contract read follows, then a4-C lands.

  - Draft verdict: `draftPublishJudgement` builds `refusals` exactly as before. The connector findings go into `advisories` only, only when `singular === 'flow'`, and each one has `severity: 'warning'`. `draftPublishVerdict` returns `.refusals`, so it does not change.

The `message` and `fix` templates are the same text. `userMessage` is `buildProbeUserMessage(code, params, userTextLocales)`, which is what the probe's `say` closure called. `labelIn` reads the same label with the same locale.   - The person's sentence (`userMessage`) is pinned: zh-CN here, and in the catalog pins in `build-probes-user-message.test.ts`.

Both already reach the step's run failure (`connector-nodes.ts`) and the package publish's probe report. The draft verdict is shown only after the `/meta` type-read check, and on MCP also after the item gate. No new kind of reader sees them.
- SQL push-down: the change reads no data. The lookups are in-memory registry calls. No finding.

### Findings

**S1 (should-fix, prose only): the public return type still says every advisory is the gate's and comes back in the publish's `advisories`.**
- The `DraftPublishJudgement` docblock in `protocol-authoring-gate.ts` says: "beside them, the gate's ADVISORIES — the findings a publish that passes returns on its 2xx … One judgement, so the two halves come from the same run of the same rules." This type is the return type of the public `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation#draftPublishJudgement`, so the docblock ships in the d.ts. The `draftPublishJudgement` docblock says the same: "with the gate's ADVISORIES beside its refusal — … which the publish returns on its 2xx".

The package publish reports it as a build-probe finding (`PublishPackageDraftsResponse.probes.issues[]`, with `code` and `fix`). The single-item publish runs no probes.

The one-line comment in `protocol.ts` ("this judgement with the gate's advisories") can be reworded on the same line, which keeps the line count, or left as it is.

**N1 (nit):** writing `Clause-②: yes (widening) — …` would record the arm for human readers. No machine reading changes, so this is optional.
**N2 (nit):** the probe `message` is not pinned verbatim. Accepted, no card (see ③).
**N3 (nit):** region step paths are not pinned. Accepted. Add the pin in the S1 delta if convenient (see ③).
